title: introduce-span-broker-and-lightweight-otel-microshim
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: our current OpenTelemetry integration in the runtime pulls a heavy, general-purpose SDK into hot paths which increases per-request allocations and CPU pressure. Multiple production incidents (high GC, OOM in low-memory tiers) traced back to span allocation churn during high-concurrency bursts. Goal: introduce a `span-broker` process and a minimal in-process Otel microshim to move expensive serialization and export work off the hot token-generation path while preserving existing semantics and sampling controls. Scope: 1) implement a tiny in-process shim (Go) that provides the minimal Span API we use (start/end, attributes, events, baggage snapshot) and uses a lock-free ring buffer to publish span deltas to the span-broker; 2) build a span-broker (same binary as runtime but a separate goroutine) that batches, serializes, and forwards to configured exporters (OTLP, internal multiplexers) asynchronously; 3) add a runtime feature flag to toggle microshim+broker; 4) integrate adaptive sampling hooks at the broker level so sampling decisions can be deferred off hot paths; 5) migration plan and fallout: compatibility layer to fall back to the legacy Otel SDK when the flag is off or when a downstream exporter requires full SDK semantics. Non-goals: replacing full Otel SDK in user agents or changing external telemetry schema.
acceptance_criteria: Total per-request allocations in the runtime hot path reduced by >= 60% on the benchmark (k8s-compact profile)
p95 tail latency of simple generate requests unchanged (+/- 5ms) under 10k rps with realistic token distributions
Broker batching reduces exporter call frequency by >= 5x relative to baseline
Feature flag exists with gradual rollout and automatic rollback on increased error rates
No change in existing trace IDs and span parentage for sampled traces (compatibility validated via golden traces)
implementation_notes: Use a bounded lock-free SPSC ring buffer per core to avoid global mutexes; fall back to a small mutex-protected buffer for older Go runtimes
Span payloads in the ring buffer should be compact: attribute keys interned via integer IDs, string dedupe via transient string table per-batch
Broker batching uses size+time heuristics: flush when batch >= 512 spans or elapsed >= 50ms
Integrate with existing exporter multiplexor so broker can route to internal telemetry pipeline and third-party OTLP endpoints
Provide a debug endpoint /internal/telemetry/trace-broker-stats that emits queue depth, batch latencies, and last-error for observability
Maintain a fallback path: if broker queue is > 95% full, fall back to synchronous minimal export for high-priority spans (sampling marker) to avoid unbounded loss
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: new codepath accidentally drops spans under extreme load -> Mitigation: conservative default sampling and queue-pressure fallback; add throttled shed metrics and alert on shed-rate>0.5%
Risk: increased binary size/attack surface -> Mitigation: microshim is pure-Go, no cgo, split symbol table and enable build tags to exclude in restricted builds
Risk: semantic mismatch with full Otel SDK -> Mitigation: compatibility tests against golden traces and an integration test matrix exercising baggage, links, and events
Risk: exporter backpressure -> Mitigation: broker implements exponential backoff per-exporter and local dead-letter queue with short TTL
plan: Week 1: prototype ring buffer + microshim API and benchmark allocations (local k6 profile)
Week 2: implement broker batching and integrate with internal exporter multiplexor; add stats endpoint
Week 3: add feature flag, end-to-end tests, and compatibility golden traces; begin dogfood in staging
Week 4: staged rollout to low-traffic clusters with canary monitoring and automatic rollback rule
Week 5: monitor for 7 days, collect metrics, finalize performance tuning and ship runtime-1.27
Post-ship: roll out to Dedicated and Private, provide migration notes to SRE and Solutions teams
